question.prompt: A function \(f\) is defined by \(f(z) = i\overline{z},\) where \(i = \sqrt{-1}\) and \(\overline{z}\) is the complex conjugate of \(z.\) How many values of \(z\) satisfy both \(|z| = 5\) and \(f(z) = z?\)

solutions.explanation:
Write \(z=x+yi\), where \(x\) and \(y\) are real. This makes conjugation and multiplication by \(i\) explicit:
\[
f(z)=i(x-yi)=y+xi.
\]
Equality of complex numbers requires equality of their real and imaginary parts. Thus \(f(z)=z\) is equivalent to \(x=y\).

The modulus condition is \(x^2+y^2=25\). Substituting \(y=x\) gives
\[
2x^2=25,\qquad x=\pm\frac{5}{\sqrt2}.
\]
Consequently the complete list is
\[
z=\frac{5}{\sqrt2}(1+i)
\quad\text{or}\quad
z=-\frac{5}{\sqrt2}(1+i).
\]
Both have equal real and imaginary parts and modulus \(5\), so both satisfy the original conditions. The two real roots above exhaust all possibilities. There are \(\boxed{2}\) values, choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
solutions.title: Compare real and imaginary parts
